editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a scary orphanage where the people meant to protect you are actually the villains. You will see how the mean matrons run a secret business, selling young girls to a creepy doctor with a scarred face. He is not trying to heal anyone, though. Instead, he uses these girls for scary brain experiments to see how far he can push the human mind. The vibe is very dark and gritty, making you feel the panic of the girls who have nowhere left to run. It feels like a nightmare that you just cannot wake up from.

What really works here is the gross-out factor and the tension. While some of the acting feels a bit old-school, the shock value is still high. The pacing starts slow but picks up once the surgeries begin. If you love old-school horror that does not hold back, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a restored 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture. If you are in a rush, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to see if you can handle the gore.
endingExplained: The movie ends in a bloody clash when the girls finally fight back against their captors. The disfigured doctor tries to perform one last surgery, but his plans fail miserably. In a fitting twist, the doctor meets a violent end, often involving the same kind of pain he put others through. The corrupt matrons are also stopped, ensuring the cycle of abuse ends. It wraps up with a feeling of relief as the survivors escape the house of horrors.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty 70s horror and mad scientist stories.
